title: Comparison between metamixr and RoBMA

title: Comparison between metamixr and RoBMA
text: Next simulate publication bias using sim_mix. Studies significant expected direction (p > .05 one-sided test) published probability 0.2, marginally significant studies (.025 < p < .05) probability 0.5, significant studies probability 1. Let’s plot distribution z statistics visually inspect simulated publciation bias. two packages state cutoffs differently. metamixr takes cumulative probabilities standard normal distribution, steps = c(0.95, 0.975), qnorm(steps) cutoffs z-statistic. Stan needs starting values for the underlying parameters of the model: the first   # mean mu1 and the gap to the second mean, tau, theta, and the   # simplex omega_raw whose cumulative sum gives the selection weights omega.   med <- function(p) median(draws[, chains, p])   centre <- list(     mu1       = med("mu1"),     mu_gap    = med("mu_gap[1]"),     tau       = c(med("tau[1]"), med("tau[2]")),     theta     = c(med("theta[1]"), med("theta[2]")),     omega_raw = c(med("omega_raw[1]"), med("omega_raw[2]"), med("omega_raw[3]")))   # one slightly perturbed copy of the centre per chain, so that the chains do not   # start from identical points   lapply(seq_len(n_chains), function(i) {     # multiplicative jitter of about +/- 5%, which keeps positive quantities positive     j <- function(x) x * exp(rnorm(length(x), 0, jitter))     theta <- j(centre$theta)     omega_raw <- j(centre$omega_raw)     list(mu1       = centre$mu1 + rnorm(1, 0, 0.01),   # renormalise: theta is a simplex          omega_raw = as.array(omega_raw / sum(omega_raw)))    # renormalise: omega_raw is a simplex   }) } set.seed(1) fits <- list() for (b in sort(unique(basin))) {   fits[[paste0("mode", b)]] <- sel_mix(y, sd, M = 2, steps = c(0.5, 0.975),                                        init = basin_inits(draws, which(basin == b)),                                        chains = 4, cores = 4, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000,                                        seed = 1, refresh = 0) } #> Warning: There were 190 divergent transitions after warmup. M number mixture components. mu numeric vector length M: mean true effect component. tau numeric vector length M: -study standard deviation true effects within component. steps cutoffs p-value intervals, format sel_mix() (cumulative probabilities standard normal distribution; e.g. c(0.95, 0.975) one-sided p-values .05 .025, .e. two-sided .10 .05 expected direction). Strictly increasing values (0, 1). weights publication probabilities p-value intervals, vector length length(steps) + 1 values [0, 1]. first element applies least significant interval, e.g. c(0.2, 0.5, 1). one_sided TRUE selection depends one-sided p-value (z-statistic y/sd), FALSE two-sided p-value (abs(y/sd)). thetas mixing weights components; defaults equal weights.
